plan.title: bug(hooks,session): an idle session's applying-host claim blocks other-provider lifecycle commands with no lease behind it, and the deny names the wrong id

narratives.Description: bug(hooks,session): an idle session's applying-host claim blocks other-provider lifecycle commands with no lease behind it, and the deny names the wrong id
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

An idle or read-only session claims `.deft/applying-host.json` just by starting or resuming, with no occupancy lease and no mutation intent. From then on, every bare lifecycle command from a different host provider in the same checkout is denied, and the deny text tells that caller to re-run with the recorded owner's session id, which is the cross-owner republish #6101 forbids. Nothing ever clears the record except an overwrite or the 8h stale window. Observed 2026-11-09 on this repo's primary: a Claude session resumed after compaction, published a claim at 16:13Z, did GitHub-only work, and a Grok session working the same checkout spent its PreToolUse budget on identity-conflict denies until the file was deleted by hand.

This is the no-lease case. #5913 is the dead-owner-with-live-lease case, #6101 is read-only overwrite of a live owner, #5917 is non-interactive primary claims. None of them covers a claim that is never backed by a lease.

## Evidence

1. `tryPublishApplyingHostFromSessionStart` (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`) publishes on every SessionStart unless a foreign live lease exists. Resume after compaction counts. There is no intent check: a session that only reads or only talks to GitHub still claims.
2. `evaluateApplyingHostLifecycleAdmission` (`packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts`) returns `foreign-owner` for a bare command from another provider whenever the record is fresh, whether or not any lease exists. The message is "Re-run with `--session-id=<applyingHostSessionId>`", the recorded owner's id, not the caller's.
3. No verb removes the record. `occupancy:release` and `session:end` leave it in place; grep finds no `rmSync` or `unlink` of `applyingHostPath`. Repair paths are republish-or-wait.
4. The primary's `.deft/ritual-state.json` named a `host:grok` owner at the same time applying-host named `host:claude`. Two identity surfaces on one checkout disagreed and neither verb could reconcile them.
5. The hook deny for the Grok session is returned quickly, so this produces deny volume rather than timeouts, but every deny is a wasted PreToolUse round and the recovery it names is the wrong one.

## Expected

- A fresh applying-host record with no occupancy lease behind it is advisory, not binding. A bare lifecycle command from another provider should take the record over (republish in its own name) when no live lease exists, instead of being denied.
- The record is cleared by `session:end` and by `occupancy:release` when the caller owns it, and there is a supported `applying-host:release` (or `session:release-stale` from #5913) for the owner to drop a claim without a hand edit.
- The deny text names the caller's own canonical id and the takeover or wait path, never the recorded owner's id. This is the same hint fix #5913 asks for.
- SessionStart publish is reinforcement when a lease exists and a soft claim otherwise; a read-only session's SessionStart should not win over a different provider's existing fresh record on the same checkout.

## Related

- #5913 dead owner holds claim for the TTL; wrong repair hint
- #6101 read-only recovery overwrote live owner (closed)
- #5917 non-interactive primary claim
- #5676 origin of applying-host
- #3742 tracker (delivery and reporting rows)

## Acceptance

1. Two genuine host sessions A (Claude) and B (Grok) on one checkout. A resumes with no lease and no mutation. B runs a bare `session:start`: B's claim replaces A's and B is not denied.
2. Same setup but A holds a live lease: B is denied, and the message names B's own id and the wait or release path, not A's id.
3. `session:end` and `occupancy:release` by the owner remove `.deft/applying-host.json`.
4. A test enumerates applying-host deny messages and fails if any one prints a session id other than the caller's.

Filed for @MScottAdams
narratives.UserStory: As a multi-host operator, I want idle no-lease applying-host claims not to block other providers, and deny text to name my caller id.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: Make no-lease applying-host advisory with takeover; fix deny text; clear on end/release; soften SessionStart without lease.

## In plain English
Pin-read confirms SessionStart always publishes and foreign-owner fires without requiring a live lease, while deny text names the owner's id. Prefer-A matches the issue Expected: advisory no-lease takeover, clear on end/release, caller-named deny.

## Findings

### blocks-the-design: foreign-owner does not require a live lease
- Evidence: `evaluateApplyingHostLifecycleAdmission` (occupancy.ts ~697+) returns `foreign-owner` when deposit host ≠ record.provider and named ≠ applyingHostSessionId, with no `liveOccupant` null check before that deny. Pin `50115917c7afb7485a1780cfef3a831de62d7270`.
- Failure mode: idle Claude claim blocks bare Grok lifecycle with no lease behind it.
- Disposition: Prefer-A — no-lease fresh record is advisory; other provider bare lifecycle republishes.

### blocks-the-design: deny names owner's id
- Evidence: foreign-owner message `Re-run with --session-id=` (same function). That is the cross-owner republish #6101 forbids.
- Failure mode: recovery hint tells B to impersonate A.
- Disposition: Prefer-A — deny names caller's canonical id and takeover/wait path.

### blocks-the-design: no clear path
- Evidence: issue Evidence 3; `publishApplyingHost` writes/replaces; SessionStart `tryPublishApplyingHostFromSessionStart` publishes; grep shows no owner clear of applying-host on session:end / occupancy:release.
- Failure mode: hand-delete or 8h stale only.
- Disposition: Prefer-A — clear on session:end / occupancy:release; supported applying-host:release.

### sharpens-framing: SessionStart publish has no intent/lease gate
- Evidence: `tryPublishApplyingHostFromSessionStart` publishes unless foreign live lease (dispatcher); compact resume counts.
- Disposition: Bound limb P4 — soft claim without lease; RO SessionStart must not win over different provider's fresh record.

### footnote: keep-outs
- #5913 live-lease dead owner; #6101 closed; #5917; #5676.

## Bound remedy
- No-lease fresh applying-host is advisory; other-provider bare lifecycle takes over (republish) — relieves: P1
- Deny names caller's canonical id and takeover/wait path, never owner's id — relieves: P2
- `session:end` / `occupancy:release` clear applying-host; supported `applying-host:release` — relieves: P3
- SessionStart soft claim without lease; RO SessionStart must not displace different-provider fresh record — relieves: P4
